Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and the esteemed members of the Joint Standing

I

My name is Jim Libby, and I am the State Senator representing District # 22, comprised of the
towns of Naples, Sebago, Baldwin, and Standish in Cumberland County; Hiram and Porter in Oxford County; and Limington, Limerick, Cornish, Parsonsfield, Newfield, Acton, and Shapleigh, in the County of York.

It is my honor to bring to your attention the contents of L.D. 685, "Resolve, to Rename the Mill
Pond Bridge the Sebago Veterans Memorial Bridge."

This bill seeks to honor those who have served in our armed forces by renaming the Mill Pond
(Bridge 6230), the Sebago Veterans Memorial Bridge

I am providing the letter of approval from the Town of Sebago for you today. The Sebago Select
Board voted unanimously in favor of this change.
I hope you join me in recognizing the brave men and woman who fought to protect our country
'
by renaming this bridge after them.

Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132"" Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither For Nor Against
LD 685, Resolve, to Rename the Mill Pond Bridge the Sebago Veterans Memorial Bridge
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 685.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for this bridge. MaineDOT's
current inventory number for this structure is 6230.
Thank you.
